validation_tag_definitions.mechanistically accurate and clinically: Supported by clinical trial data and mechanistic understanding
validation_tag_definitions.mechanistically accurate only: Biologically plausible based on mechanism but lacks clinical validation
validation_tag_definitions.mechanistically rare: Possible but uncommon or unusual scenario
validation_tag_definitions.mechanistically not possible: Contradicts known biology or mechanism of action

sensitive_upregulation.description: High EGFR signaling at baseline indicates active oncogenic driver mutations (e.g., EGFR exon 19 deletions) which are known to be sensitive to afatinib, an irreversible EGFR inhibitor.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Low baseline EGFR signaling might indicate compensatory pathways or partial inhibition by endogenous factors, yet tumors with specific EGFR mutations can still respond to afatinib.

resistant_upregulation.description: High EGFR signaling with resistance suggests secondary mutations (e.g., T790M) or activation of bypass pathways (e.g., MET amplification) that confer resistance to afatinib.

resistant_downregulation.description: Low EGFR signaling with resistance may indicate reliance on alternative oncogenic pathways or prior treatment effects leading to pathway suppression.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Afatinib effectively inhibits EGFR signaling, but compensatory upregulation may occur in sensitive tumors due to feedback loops, yet overall pathway activity remains suppressed.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Afatinib leads to sustained downregulation of EGFR signaling in sensitive tumors, resulting in tumor regression and clinical response.

resistant_upregulation.description: In resistant tumors, afatinib may initially suppress EGFR but alternative pathways (e.g., MET, HER2) become upregulated, maintaining oncogenic signaling.

resistant_downregulation.description: Afatinib may reduce EGFR signaling, but resistance mechanisms (e.g., persistent downstream signaling) prevent effective tumor control.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Upregulation of the ERK pathway in lung cancer often indicates active EGFR signaling, which afatinib can effectively inhibit, leading to tumor sensitivity.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Downregulation of the ERK pathway may indicate reliance on alternative pathways, but residual EGFR signaling could still render tumors sensitive to afatinib.

resistant_upregulation.description: Upregulation of the ERK pathway with resistance suggests alternative pathway activation or mutations downstream of EGFR, reducing afatinib efficacy.

resistant_downregulation.description: Downregulation of the ERK pathway in resistant tumors may indicate bypass signaling or compensatory mechanisms independent of EGFR.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Afatinib treatment in sensitive tumors may initially upregulate ERK as a feedback response, but sustained inhibition of EGFR eventually downregulates the pathway, leading to tumor regression.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Afatinib effectively inhibits EGFR, leading to sustained downregulation of the ERK pathway and tumor regression in sensitive tumors.

resistant_upregulation.description: In resistant tumors, afatinib may fail to inhibit the ERK pathway due to compensatory signaling or mutations, maintaining pathway activity despite treatment.

resistant_downregulation.description: Afatinib may downregulate the ERK pathway in resistant tumors, but resistance mechanisms may involve alternative pathways or mutations that sustain tumor survival.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Upregulation of the HGF/MET/RAS/ERK pathway indicates active signaling that drives tumor growth, making it susceptible to afatinib, which inhibits EGFR and HER2, reducing downstream signaling.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Downregulation suggests low pathway activity, but sensitivity may arise from dependency on alternative EGFR signaling, which afatinib effectively targets.

resistant_upregulation.description: Despite upregulation, resistance may occur due to compensatory activation of parallel pathways like PI3K/AKT, bypassing afatinib's effects.

resistant_downregulation.description: Low pathway activity with resistance suggests reliance on non-EGFR pathways or mutations conferring afatinib resistance.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Afatinib treatment in sensitive tumors typically downregulates this pathway, but upregulation post-treatment may reflect compensatory mechanisms or tumor adaptation.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Effective afatinib treatment results in downregulation of the pathway, correlating with tumor regression and clinical response.

resistant_upregulation.description: Persistent upregulation post-afatinib indicates resistance, potentially due to MET amplification or alternative pathway activation.

resistant_downregulation.description: Downregulation in resistant tumors suggests initial pathway inhibition, but resistance mechanisms like secondary mutations or bypass signaling maintain tumor viability.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Upregulation of VEGF signaling in lung cancer may indicate high angiogenic activity, which can be disrupted by afatinib's EGFR inhibition, leading to reduced tumor vascularization and growth.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Downregulation of VEGF signaling suggests low angiogenic dependency, but afatinib may still be effective due to its primary action on EGFR mutations driving tumor growth.

resistant_upregulation.description: High VEGF signaling could drive angiogenesis independent of EGFR, leading to resistance as afatinib primarily targets EGFR-driven pathways.

resistant_downregulation.description: Low VEGF signaling with resistance suggests alternative pathways or mutations (e.g., MET amplification) are driving tumor growth, reducing afatinib efficacy.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Afatinib treatment may paradoxically increase VEGF signaling as a compensatory mechanism, but overall tumor reduction occurs due to effective EGFR pathway inhibition.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Effective inhibition of EGFR by afatinib leads to decreased VEGF signaling, reducing angiogenesis and tumor growth.

resistant_upregulation.description: Persistent upregulation of VEGF signaling post-treatment indicates a bypass mechanism, potentially involving alternative angiogenic pathways, maintaining resistance.

resistant_downregulation.description: Despite VEGF signaling reduction, resistance persists due to other oncogenic pathways or mutations sustaining tumor growth.

sensitive_upregulation.description: Upregulation of the AKT pathway suggests active signaling, which may drive EGFR-mutant lung cancer proliferation. Afatinib, an EGFR inhibitor, can effectively block upstream signaling, reducing AKT pathway activity and tumor growth.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Downregulation of the AKT pathway may indicate reliance on alternative pathways for survival. Afatinib's inhibition of EGFR can further suppress compensatory signaling, leading to tumor regression.

resistant_upregulation.description: Persistent upregulation of the AKT pathway suggests activation of bypass signaling routes, such as PI3K mutations, conferring resistance to afatinib despite EGFR inhibition.

resistant_downregulation.description: Downregulation of the AKT pathway in resistant tumors may indicate reliance on other survival pathways, such as MET or HER2, which are not targeted by afatinib.

sensitive_upregulation.description: In sensitive tumors, afatinib reduces AKT pathway activity by inhibiting EGFR, but transient upregulation may occur due to feedback loops before sustained suppression.

sensitive_downregulation.description: Afatinib effectively suppresses the AKT pathway in sensitive tumors, leading to decreased cell proliferation and increased apoptosis.

resistant_upregulation.description: In resistant tumors, afatinib fails to suppress AKT pathway upregulation due to compensatory mechanisms, such as activation of alternative receptor tyrosine kinases.

resistant_downregulation.description: Afatinib treatment may not affect the already downregulated AKT pathway in resistant tumors, as resistance mechanisms are independent of EGFR signaling.
